Articles are words like a, an, and the. We use them before nouns to make sentences clearer. For example, in the sentence "I deposit to bank," the word THE or A is missing. If you say "I deposit to THE bank," it means a particular bank. If you say "I deposit to A bank," it means any bank, not a specific one. Using THE and A makes your sentence clear and exact. Not using them makes the sentence more general.

The benefit of learning and using articles is that it improves his writing and speaking skills. It makes his sentences more correct and easier to understand. In his Caterpillar sentences, he missed using articles sometimes, which can make his sentences unclear or grammatically incorrect. When he correctly uses articles, his sentences will sound better and be easier for others to understand. Practicing this will help him write more accurately and confidently.
